infoPlist.NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription: Sharing your location lets the rider find your door, and lets us check the address is inside the delivery area. It is optional — a typed address is enough.

plugins.locationAlwaysAndWhenInUsePermission: Sharing your location lets the rider find your door. It is optional — a typed address is enough.

plugins.//: Unlike the rider app, this one ships a purpose-made 96x96 transparent notification icon. Android renders the icon as a white silhouette of whatever it is given, so the app icon would come out an unrecognisable blob; a flat bolt on transparency silhouettes correctly. `color` is the accent Android tints it with, and `defaultChannel` must match CHANNEL_ID in edawr-backend/api/push.py — a mismatch is silent.

extra.//: apiUrl is the backend a RELEASE build talks to. Development ignores it and auto-detects the dev machine's LAN IP instead (see src/config.ts). Leaving it null makes a release build fail loudly at startup rather than silently calling localhost — set it, or pass EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL at build time.
extra.//push: Push needs an EAS project id, which `eas init` writes here as extra.eas.projectId. Until it exists src/push.ts declines to register and the app runs normally on the tracker's ten-second poll — a build with no project id is a working store that cannot be buzzed, which is a gap and not a failure. The backend half also has to be switched on (PUSH_ENABLED=true) with FCM/APNs credentials uploaded; see edawr-backend/api/push.py.
extra.//cleartext: There is deliberately no android.usesCleartextTraffic here, so cleartext stays OFF (the Android 9+ default). src/config.ts refuses an http:// API URL in a release build for the same reason: the customer's password and bearer token would otherwise cross the network in plaintext. (This key lives under extra because Expo validates the android block against a schema and rejects unknown properties.)
